item.title: Waymo conquered city streets — why does it keep stumbling on freeways?
item.description:
Most people know not to try to pass highway patrol cars while performing a traffic break on a freeway. But on November 6th, a driverless Waymo on Interstate 280 failed that test.

Video shows the robotaxi attempting to overtake two California Highway Patrol cruisers during a traffic break, a moving violation that could get a human driver's license suspended. For Waymo, it was the latest in a series of freeway blunders that eventually led to the California DMV last week banning its vehicles from all state interstates.

item.title: X is finally getting its first parental controls
item.description:
X is finally rolling out parental controls that allow parents and guardians to manage teens' accounts on the platform. While teens will retain ownership of their own account, parents and guardians will be able to see how much time their child has spent on X, set daily limits, require approval for new followers, and limit For You recommendations to accounts a teen already follows.

item.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
item.description:
A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts - more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors - with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold."

item.title: Now Google’s Familiar Faces AI feature works on Walmart’s $35 smart home camera too
item.description:
A couple of Walmart's budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google's familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required to access the feature.

Both cameras and Google's Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd gen) also have a new remote control in the Google Home app you can use to start or stop a 30-second security siren while watching the camera's live video feed.

item.title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
item.description:
Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods, not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products.

item.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
item.description:
Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market.

item.title: WhatsApp’s new scheduled messages let you choose the right time to send
item.description:
WhatsApp's 3 billion users are getting an option that Meta says is one of the most requested features, with the ability to schedule messages in advance for both private conversations and group chats. Most messaging platforms have had this for a very long time, but now it's on WhatsApp too.

If you think of a text at an inconvenient time or don't want to forget to fire off a birthday message at 4AM, you can draft it and set it to send anywhere from 10 minutes to two weeks later. The feature works with photos and videos, too.

item.title: EPA reports ‘zero’ airborne lead following controlled Army detonation in Iowa
item.description:
Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. Videos of the detonation showed plumes of smoke several hundred feet high drifting south before quickly dissipating.

item.title: 1Password breach leaked customer names and emails, but not passwords
item.description:
1Password says a hacker stole customer names and email addresses after gaining access to its backend systems. The breach didn't expose passwords or other information stored in customer vaults, but could put users at risk of phishing attempts, according to a post disclosing the incident. It's unclear how many users are affected.

The password manager began investigating the incident on November 19th, after an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account.
